conviction_note: Q1 is a guided quarter ($195-200M operating income) that the company has recently landed inside rather than beaten, so the quarter itself carries little. The move will turn on the FY27 $850-880M reaffirm or raise and on the 10:00 call's aerospace tone, after a 40% drawdown and a sector that sold GE's beat-and-raise on 10-20. I lean slightly up (p_up 52) on a 7% absolute move, because I trust history and sector moves over a 12.9% option implied move built on a thin, wide chain. The findings sum to +0.9. The scaled number is smaller because the sector-reaction evidence offsets the fundamentals inside p_up.
bar: Company guide for Q1 FY27: consolidated operating income $195-200M (SAO $218-222M, PEP $6-7M), from the Q4 FY26 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17843/000001784326000030/a4thqtr2026resultspressrel.htm, and the presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17843/000001784326000028/a4q26earningspresentatio.htm. At Q4's interest (~$6M), other income and a ~21% tax rate on 50.2M shares, that implies about $3.05-3.10 EPS. EPS estimates disagree: finviz EPS next Q 3.04 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CRS), MarketBeat $2.91 from one estimate (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CRS/earnings/). I sized against the company guide. FY27 operating-income guide is $850-880M, adjusted FCF $400-430M.
positioning_check: Short float 2.99%, short ratio 1.95 days, short interest 1.44M shares; institutional ownership 95.6%; insider transactions -8.57% (finviz, as of 2026-10-21, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CRS). Not a crowded short. Baseline 25d skew -2.64 vol points (upside paid, small), put/call OI 0.43 on total OI of only 1,779 with an ATM spread of 21% of mid, so the 12.91% event-implied move rests on a thin chain. Spot 363.95 is -41% from the 52-week high (~$626 intraday, week of 2026-07-06), -7.9% over 20 days, -4.2% over 5 days; 20d realised vol 20.6%.

findings.finding: The reported quarter is pre-guided at $195-200M consolidated operating income (SAO $218-222M, PEP $6-7M). Recent prints landed inside the guide: Q4 FY26 at $206.9M against $205-210M, FY26 at $702M against $700-705M. The bar is about $3.05-3.10 implied EPS, against finviz 3.04 and a single MarketBeat estimate of 2.91. I expect operating income near $199M, about 1% over the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 landed inside its guide (206.9 vs 205-210) and the stock rose +3.17% the next session (2026-07-31), after a -5.1% event day that started with a gap down. Q3 FY26 'exceeded guidance' and the move was +5.33% (baseline). All eight recorded reactions are positive, though the history rows are duplicated and session-tagged inconsistently.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, because the company told the market the number. What is open is landing inside or above the range. A priced miss would show up as estimates below the guide, and finviz sits at the guide. Only the stale one-estimate MarketBeat figure sits below it.

findings.finding: GE Aerospace's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20) is a direct downstream read for CRS, which makes 66% of ex-surcharge sales in Aerospace & Defense. GE reported material input from priority suppliers up double digits year on year, orders +49%, and a 2026 CES operating-profit guide raised to $10.5-10.6B from $10.25-10.35B. The offset: LEAP deliveries grew only +5% in Q3 against +26% year to date, and GE agreed to buy castings maker CPP. Net, this supports demand for CRS's superalloy volumes and pricing commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26, CRS Aerospace & Defense sales rose +17% year on year, management said 'strong pricing environment' continues, and the stock rose +3.17% the next day. I have no per-line reaction history for a peer read.
findings.why_not_priced: The market read GE negatively: GE -3.67% on 2.1x volume, with CRS, ATI and HWM all down. If the 'supplier input up double digits' line had been priced for CRS, CRS would not have kept falling (372.53 on 10-20, about 364 intraday on 10-21). The positive supply-chain volume line looks to be lost under the LEAP deceleration headline.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, from a direct counterparty. CRS's own Q4 presentation cites higher production rates and MRO in aerospace: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17843/000001784326000028/a4q26earningspresentatio.htm. It shares the 10-20 event with the peer-reaction finding below, which covers the price reaction and not the numbers.

findings.finding: The first full-quarter guide comes under returned CEO Tony Thene, who took the role back after CEO Brian Malloy died on 2026-07-24 and was CEO 2015-2026 and author of the FY29 $1.2-1.3B target. Q1's $195-200M guide is 22.6% of the FY27 midpoint, so the rest of the year needs about $222M a quarter, near Q4's $206.9M plus pricing. The company says demand and pricing are strong and Q1 is held back by planned maintenance. A reaffirmed or raised $850-880M FY27 guide meets a stock that has fallen from about $600 to $364 since late July with no change in guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 guidance was raised during the year to $700-705M (Q3 release) and the stock rose +5.33% after that print. The FY27 guide issued with Q4 was followed by +3.17%.
findings.why_not_priced: A -41% drawdown with no guide cut, a forward P/E of 22.7 (finviz) and a $536 mean target say the market is discounting either a guide cut or a de-rating. If the market expected the guide to hold, the multiple would not have compressed from about 35x. The release is the first chance to test that.
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 presentation, with the FY27 guide, the 'not the peak' FY29 language and strong pricing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17843/000001784326000028/a4q26earningspresentatio.htm

findings.finding: Capital return during Q1 FY27: CRS completed the remaining $119.0M of its $400M buyback in August 2026 and authorised a further $1.0B on 2026-08-12, about 5.5% of a market cap of roughly $18B. The Q1 release will show Q1 repurchases of at least $119M, against $45.2M in Q4, made while the stock fell through the quarter, and may give a pace for the new program.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public. The Q1 dollars spent, and whether CRS used the drawdown aggressively, are not. A market that had priced heavy buying would not have let the stock slide on below-average volume with no support.
findings.independence: Q4 release, with $119.0M remaining at 6/30 and Q4 buyback of $45.2M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17843/000001784326000030/a4thqtr2026resultspressrel.htm

findings.finding: Insider selling into the quarter: Chairman and CEO Tony Thene sold 109,283 shares on 2026-08-25, about 19% of his 576k combined holdings and about $50M at that week's ~$476 price, which the company disclosed in an 8-K item 7.01. Form 144s were filed on 08-21, 08-25 (two) and 09-04, and finviz shows insider transactions at -8.57%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the sale was disclosed by 8-K two months ago and the stock has since fallen about 24%. Its residual weight is on how the call reads the returned CEO's commitment. It is filed small for breadth.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions show Form 144s on 2026-08-21, 08-25 and 09-04: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000017843.json

findings.finding: The sector sold a beat-and-raise on the eve of this print. On 2026-10-20, the day of GE's raise, GE closed -3.67%, ATI -3.28%, HWM -3.82% (5.5M shares, about 2x average), and CRS -1.58%. On 10-21 intraday, HWM was -3.19%, ATI -1.23% and CRS -2.1%. HWM had already fallen about 21% from its August high on a 'SpaceX/Tesla could make their own turbine blades' scare (Trefis, 2026-09-09). Aerospace-materials names are being sold into good numbers right now, which argues against a large up-reaction even on a reaffirm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CRS fell -5.1% on 2026-07-30 (gap down from 530.62 to 492.21) before its Q4 release, then rose +3.17%. Its own prints have bounced against this backdrop rather than extended it.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a reaction-function item rather than an unpriced fact. The tape shows it, and it argues the market will not pay up for a guide hold. It conflicts with the small upside skew (-2.64), which is why it is sized small. Short float is 3%, so there is no squeeze mechanism.
findings.independence: GE daily tape (-3.67% on 10-20): https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/GE?range=1mo&interval=1d ; ATI tape: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ATI?range=10d&interval=1d ; Trefis HWM blade scare: https://finance.yahoo.com/m/66329460-1388-3880-bc5e-97a1f26ef666/should-you-buy-howmet-stock.html. It shares the GE 10-20 event with the GE-numbers finding, but this one covers the reaction and that one the numbers.

baseline_tension: The small upside skew (-2.64) and the -41% drawdown leave room for a relief move on a guide hold, and my slight lean agrees with the skew. The sector tape of 10-20 and 10-21 (peers selling GE's beat-and-raise) cuts against it, so p_up is held near 50. The 12.91% implied move rests on a 1,779-OI chain with a 21% spread, and I discount it toward the name's 3-5% history.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): the quarter finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 5 (a proxy is filed smaller): the GE counterparty read cut from +0.5 to +0.4 and kept filed as a proxy.
Rule 7 (a sign against the skew needs a reason or a smaller size): the sector-selling positioning finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6. Short float is 3%, so this is not about a squeeze.
Rule 1 left the guidance finding at +0.8: this name's recent prints were bought (+3.17%, +5.33%), not sold.
